Twelve grill events exist; every one fired between zero and ninety-one seconds after its item's own create event, three within the same second, and no item body was ever revised in response to one. Twelve of twenty-four packages under internal carry no bundle at all while SPX-REPO-002 mandates one, and check answers ok. Six of the ten dogfooded defects landed in exactly those uncovered packages.

FIRST ACTION TAKEN, because it needed no new machinery: verify commands are now configured, so the gate runs go build and go test on both sides of every submit. 2. Server-computed environment differential at grill: print the live value of a fixed axis list beside what the item's tests construct. 8. Server-executed mutant-kill gate at submit. Strongest evidence generator after the first, ranked here only for its measured eighty-second tax on the package where most work happens.

Requirement, refined by the user in two steps: failed CI checks must reach the LLM through the MCP surface, and NOT as something the LLM queries — the server polls, the LLM is told. The signal arrives on whatever tool call happens next, unasked.

MECHANISM, matching what already exists rather than inventing a channel. The server already owns a piggyback path: postCall prepends sibling learnings (sw records) and the compact and stale hints to any tool result. Red CI joins it. A background poller — goroutine on the Server, interval about thirty seconds, started with the server and stopped with it — walks the items in active or done whose task branch has an open pull request, asks the forge for the head's check verdict, and stores the latest per item. postCall prepends one dense record per item whose stored verdict is failing: the ! finding grammar, naming the item in display form, the pull request number and the URL, so the LLM can act in one hop.

LATCHING, same discipline as the stale hint: a red verdict is surfaced once per crossing, re-armed when the verdict leaves failing, so a long red does not tax every call while it is being fixed — with one difference mandated by ADR-01KYDG: on the transition where the flow would have acted on the branch (done, archive), a still-red verdict is restated even if latched, because acting-adjacent silence is the ambiguity that decision forbids.

CONSTRAINTS. The poller must never hold the server mutex while talking to the forge — it snapshots what to poll under the lock, polls outside it, and writes results back under the lock, or a slow forge freezes every tool call. Offline mode answers ChecksNone for everything, so the poller idles there by construction and the tests need no forge. A forge error in the poller is stored and surfaced as its own record once — a broken poller that says nothing is the silent failure this whole line of work exists to eliminate.

TESTS. A scripted forge turning failing surfaces exactly one finding on the next tool result; staying red stays quiet on subsequent calls until re-crossing; recovering to passing re-arms; the done transition restates a latched red; the poller never runs the forge under the mutex, asserted with a lock-held probe; offline stays entirely quiet.
